Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 22b89ba178dd0a66a26699ead014a3e73ff8e044 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sandipan Das <sandipan@linux.ibm.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Feb 2021 13:37:44 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] powerpc/sstep: Fix darn emulation

Commit 8813ff49607e ("powerpc/sstep: Check instruction validity
against ISA version before emulation") introduced a proper way to skip
unknown instructions. This makes sure that the same is used for the
darn instruction when the range selection bits have a reserved value.

Fixes: a23987ef267a ("powerpc: sstep: Add support for darn instruction")
Signed-off-by: Sandipan Das <sandipan@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Michael Ellerman <mpe@ellerman.id.au>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210204080744.135785-2-sandipan@linux.ibm.com

diff --git a/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c b/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c
index 11f14b209d7f..683f7c20f74b 100644
--- a/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c
+++ b/arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c
@@ -1916,7 +1916,7 @@ int analyse_instr(struct instruction_op *op, const struct pt_regs *regs,
 				goto compute_done;
 			}
 
-			return -1;
+			goto unknown_opcode;
 #ifdef __powerpc64__
 		case 777:	/* modsd */
 			if (!cpu_has_feature(CPU_FTR_ARCH_300))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/powerpc/lib/sstep.c`**
   - The line `return -1;` was replaced with `goto unknown_opcode;`. This change alters the flow of the function to handle unknown opcodes by redirecting to a label (`unknown_opcode`) instead of returning an error code directly.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `sstep.c` is related to the previous commit that introduced a mechanism to check the validity of instructions against the ISA version. By changing the return statement to a `goto`, the code now properly handles the case of unknown instructions, specifically for the `darn` instruction when the range selection bits are reserved. This ensures that the emulation logic adheres to the updated instruction validity checks, thereby fixing the bug associated with the `darn` instruction emulation.
